extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) preparing and filing U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and required content/format for an Application Data Sheet (ADS), the order/format of application elements, and the requirements/timelines for claiming benefit/priority to earlier U.S. and foreign applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), and 386(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet title and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be titled "Application Data Sheet." If provided, the application data sheet is part of the application for which it has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ADS may be submitted in provisional, nonprovisional, nonprovisional international design, or national stage applications and must be submitted when required by § 1.55 or § 1.78 to claim priority or benefit. If an ADS is provided, it must contain all section headings listed in paragraph (b) (except as provided in paragraph (c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS must contain required bibliographic section headings
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must contain all of the section headings listed in paragraph (b) of § 1.76 with appropriate data for each section heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ADS must include the specific headings described in the rule (inventor info, correspondence info, application info, representative info, domestic benefit info, foreign priority info, applicant information). For supplemental ADSs, include the headings for each section present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor information (ADS bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor information includes the legal name, residence, and mailing address of the inventor or each joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming conventions for applicants (pre-AIA text) require family name and at least one given name without abbreviation; inventorship is governed by § 1.41 and changes by § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence information (ADS bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence information includes the correspondence address (may be indicated by reference to a customer number) to which correspondence is to be directed (see § 1.33(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing correspondence info in ADS controls correspondence routing; correspondence address changes governed by § 1.33(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application information (ADS bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application information includes the title of the invention, total number of drawing sheets, a suggested drawing figure for publication (nonprovisional), any docket number, the type of application (utility, plant, design, reissue, provisional), secrecy-order disclosure flag, and for plant applications the Latin genus/species and variety denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When previously filed application reference is required under § 1.57(a), application information should also indicate replacement of specification/drawings by the referenced prior application and identify that prior application by number, filing date, and authority. For some filing-date ranges (pre-AIA vs post-AIA), additional fields like suggested classification/Technology Center may be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative information (ADS bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative information includes the registration number of each practitioner having a power of attorney in the application (preferably by reference to a customer number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS does not itself constitute a power of attorney (see § 1.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic benefit information (ADS bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic benefit information includes the application number, filing date, status (including patent number if available), and relationship of each application for which a benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 and § 1.78 and need not otherwise be made part of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority information (ADS bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority information includes the application number, country (or intellectual property authority), and filing date of each foreign application for which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the priority claim required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and § 1.55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/assignee information (ADS bibliographic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant information includes the name and address of the legal representative, assignee, person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign, or other person showing sufficient proprietary interest who is the applicant under § 1.43 or § 1.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignment information in the ADS does not substitute for compliance with part 3 (recording assignments) of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsigned ADS will be treated only as a transmittal letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting/updating information in a previously submitted ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in a previously submitted ADS, inventor's oath/declaration, or otherwise of record may be corrected or updated until payment of the issue fee by filing a new ADS providing corrected or updated information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: inventorship changes must comply with § 1.48; foreign priority and domestic benefit information changes must comply with §§ 1.55 and 1.78; correspondence address changes governed by § 1.33(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental ADS content and formatting for changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A corrective/updated ADS may include only those sections containing changed/updated information and must include the section headings for each included section and identify the information being changed, with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for text removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of changes is not required for an ADS included with an initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371. For pre-AIA rules, supplemental ADSs must be titled "Supplemental Application Data Sheet" and include all section headings listed in paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies between ADS and other documents — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For inconsistencies between information supplied by both an ADS and other documents, the most recent submission will govern with respect to inconsistencies as between the information provided in an ADS, a designation of a correspondence address, or by the inventor's oath or declaration, subject to specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will capture bibliographic information from the ADS and generally will not review the oath/declaration to determine consistency with ADS data. Captured bibliographic information containing errors may be corrected by request and supplemental ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies — ADS governs over contemporaneous documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The information in the ADS will govern when inconsistent with the information supplied at the same time by a designation of correspondence address or the inventor's oath or declaration, and will govern when inconsistent with information supplied at any time in certain international/request forms (PCT Request Form, PLT Model International Request Form, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist (see next entry) and certain elements like foreign priority and domestic benefit have special rules where the most recent ADS governs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies — oath/declaration governs inventorship and citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration under § 1.63 or § 1.67 governs inconsistencies with the ADS in the naming of inventors (§ 1.41(a)(1)) and in setting forth their citizenship (35 U.S.C. 115).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship changes remain governed by § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Law Treaty (PLT) and PCT forms satisfy ADS requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of a priority/benefit claim in the PLT Model International Request Form or the PCT Request Form satisfies the requirement in § 1.55 or § 1.78 for presentation of such claims in an ADS; presentation of the name of the applicant in certain PLT forms satisfies § 1.46 ADS requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PCT Request Form is submitted in an application under 35 U.S.C. 111, it must be accompanied by a clear indication that treatment of the application as under 35 U.S.C. 111 is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement/order of application papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Utility application transmittal form, (2) Fee transmittal form, (3) Application data sheet, (4) Specification, (5) Drawings, (6) The inventor's oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following this order is the recommended arrangement for filing; includes ADS at third position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification section ordering and headings format
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should include sections in order (if applicable): Title; Cross-reference to related applications; Statement re federally sponsored research; Names of parties to joint research agreement; Incorporation by reference statements; Statement re prior disclosures; Background; Brief summary; Brief description of drawings; Detailed description; Claims; Abstract; and Sequence Listing (when required). Section headings should be in uppercase and without underlining or bold type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific incorporation-by-reference rules for ASCII files, XML sequence listings, and large tables reference other MPEP sections (§§ 1.52(e)(8), 1.96(c), 1.821(c), 1.831(a), 1.58(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit to a prior-filed provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) — filing-time limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application must be filed not later than twelve months after the provisional filing date to claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), subject to paragraph (b) (delayed filing restoration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, a later application may be entitled to claim the provisional benefit via 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c) of a subsequent application filed within that 12-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming provisional benefit — other substantive prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Each prior-filed provisional must name the inventor (or joint inventor) named in the later application, be entitled to a filing date per § 1.53(c), and have the basic filing fee set forth in § 1.16(d) paid within the time period set forth in § 1.53(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet these prerequisites prevents claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference requirement for claiming provisional benefit (ADS inclusion and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any nonprovisional application claiming benefit of one or more prior-filed provisionals must contain, or be amended to contain, a reference to each such provisional identifying it by provisional application number; if later-filed is a nonprovisional application, the reference must be included in an ADS (§ 1.76(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference must be submitted during the pendency of the later-filed application and, for 111(a) applications, also within the later of four months from the actual filing date or sixteen months from the provisional filing date (special timing for national stage entries under 35 U.S.C. 371). Failure to timely submit is considered a waiver of benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), except as provided in paragraph (c) for delayed/unintentional filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior provisional was filed in a language other than English and an English translation and statement of accuracy were not previously filed, the applicant will be notified and given time to file the translation and statement in the provisional application. A timely reply must include confirmation that translation and statement were filed in the provisional, or an ADS eliminating the reference, or the nonprovisional will be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation and statement may be filed in the provisional even if it has become abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement requirement for mixed pre/post-March 16, 2013 effective filing-date claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional filed on or after March 16, 2013 claims the benefit of a provisional filed prior to March 16, 2013 and also contains (or contained) a claim having an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, the applicant must provide a statement to that effect within specified timing (later of 4 months from filing, 4 months from national stage entry, 16 months from provisional, or the date a first post-March 16, 2013 claim is presented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant is not required to provide the statement if they reasonably believe (per § 1.56(c)) that the application does not and did not contain a claim with effective filing date on/after March 16, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed filing restoration (within two months) and petition content
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subsequent nonprovisional has a filing date after the 12-month period but within two months after it, benefit of the provisional may be restored under PCT Rule 26bis.3 (for international apps) or upon petition if the delay was unintentional. A petition filed on/after May 13, 2015 must be filed in the subsequent application and include: (i) the reference to the provisional (ADS), (ii) the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)), and (iii) a statement that the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information to assess whether the delay was unintentional. Restoration under PCT Rule 26bis.3 does not relieve the requirement to include the reference in a national-stage application within the § 1.78(a)(4) time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentionally delayed claim acceptance (provisional) — petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) is presented after the time period in § 1.78(a)(4), the claim may be accepted if the reference was unintentionally delayed; a petition to accept must be accompanied by the reference, the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)), and a statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) — acceptable prior-filed application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Each prior-filed application relied upon under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) must name the inventor (or joint inventor) named in the later application and must be: (i) an international application entitled to a filing date under PCT Article 11 and designating the U.S.; (ii) an international design application entitled to a filing date under § 1.1023 and designating the U.S.; or (iii) a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) entitled to a filing date under § 1.53(b) or (d) with the basic filing fee paid within the pendency of that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued prosecution applications filed under § 1.53(d) are excepted from certain requirements (see paragraph (d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: References to prior nonprovisional/international applications (35 U.S.C. 120 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed nonprovisional, international, or international design application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) must contain or be amended to contain a reference to each such prior-filed application identifying it by application number, international application number and filing date, or international registration number and filing date; if later-filed is a nonprovisional, the reference must be included in an ADS (§ 1.76(b)(5)). The reference must also identify the relationship (continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference and applicable fee (§ 1.17(w)) must be submitted during pendency of the later-filed application; for 111(a) apps also within later of 4 months from actual filing or 16 months from prior-filed application's filing date. Failure to timely submit is considered waiver except as provided in paragraph (e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for a continued prosecution application (CPA) as specific reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for a continued prosecution application under § 1.53(d) is the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 to the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of an application by application number is the identification of every application assigned that number necessary for the specific reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references limitation in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-references to other related applications may be made when appropriate, but cross-references to applications for which a benefit is not claimed under title 35 must not be included in an ADS (§ 1.76(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only applications for which you are claiming the statutory benefit in the ADS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy and translation requirement for foreign-originated international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) to an international application or international design application that designates but did not originate in the United States, the Office may require a certified copy of such application together with an English translation if filed in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to supply certified copies/translations when claiming benefit to such foreign-originated international applications.
